sentence: This project studies whether immune cells and the genes active in them are linked to mild cognitive impairment and dementia in African American adults.
This project studies how affective information in the environments of children shapes word learning, including for children with depressed caregivers.
This project tests whether a urine-based DNA test detects more tumor DNA than matched blood tests in patients with early-stage oropharyngeal cancer.
This project studies how a certain protein works in different types of cells to shape the immune response to melanoma.
This project provides tools and expertise for studying genomics, proteomics and metabolomics in environmental health research.
This project studies how developing nerve cells mature and how they organize their chromatin during that process.
This project studies how cells regulate microtubule acetylation and vertex strength while they migrate through junctional barriers in a living system.
This project studies circulating tumor cells from breast cancer patients to understand why cancers stop responding to hormonal therapy.
This project studies brain states linked to high and low performance in the cerebellum, an area of the brain involved in motor and cognitive functions.
This project studies the role of resident memory T cells in primary melanoma and skin immune responses.
This project studies how physical constriction affects cancer stem cells that spread, including their survival in the lung.
This project studies a protein that directly regulates senescence to better understand back pain linked to intervertebral disc disorders.
This project collects, checks and stores plasmids containing genes and shares them with researchers around the world.
This project studies how cytochrome P450 enzymes change how active cancer-causing chemicals and drugs are in the body.
This project builds hemoglobin-based biomaterials that deliver oxygen to help stem cells work better in osteoarthritis.
This project tests an imaging method that measures blood flow in skeletal muscles of the lower extremities in peripheral artery disease.
This project studies how screen media activity such as videogaming and texting relates to mental health and brain development in children and adolescents.
This project studies how the immune system fights tumors and builds therapies based on tumor immunology.
This project studies how a certain protein helps keep mitochondria and the heart healthy during aging.
This project builds a foundation model that analyzes live cell imaging data to characterize cellular morphodynamics.
